overview.short: Kolkata, the City of Joy and cultural capital of India, is famed for colonial grand marble monuments, cantilever river bridges, historic tramways, and vibrant intellectual heritage.
overview.description: Kolkata, nestled on the eastern bank of the sacred Hooghly River in West Bengal, is India's historic capital and artistic nerve centre. From the regal British-era white marble splendour of the Victoria Memorial to the engineering marvel of Howrah Bridge, spiritual solace at Dakshineswar Kali Temple, and iconic yellow Ambassador taxis bustling down wide tree-lined boulevards, Kolkata charms travellers with its unmatched intellectual and festive soul.
overview.about: Kolkata is the cultural and literary soul of India, celebrated worldwide as the City of Joy. Adorned with monumental colonial architecture, sacred riverfront ghats, iconic yellow taxis, and grand cultural festivals like Durga Puja, it offers an indelible sensory journey.

topPlaces.name: Victoria Memorial
topPlaces.distance: In Kolkata Centre, Queens Way, Maidan
topPlaces.description: Grand Indo-Saracenic white Makrana marble palace commemorating Queen Victoria, surrounded by 64 acres of royal landscaped gardens, reflection pools, and 25 galleries of rare art and colonial artifacts.
topPlaces.travelTime: Centrally located on the Maidan, accessible by Maidan or Rabindra Sadan Metro

topPlaces.name: Howrah Bridge (Rabindra Setu)
topPlaces.description: World-famous suspended balance cantilever steel bridge engineered without nuts or bolts over the Hooghly River, carrying over 100,000 vehicles and 150,000 pedestrians daily.
topPlaces.travelTime: 5 mins drive from BBD Bagh or Howrah Railway Terminus

topPlaces.name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
topPlaces.distance: 14 km north of Kolkata city centre
topPlaces.description: Venerated 19th-century Navaratna nine-spire temple on the Hooghly riverbank founded by Rani Rashmoni, sacred for its association with mystic saint Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and 12 riverside Shiva shrines.
topPlaces.travelTime: 25 mins from Central Kolkata via Kolkata Metro Blue Line to Dakshineswar

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Kolkata?
faq.a: The best time to visit Kolkata is Oct – Mar. Summers are 28–36°C and winters are 14–28°C.

The nearest airport is Kolkata / nearest airport (30 km) and the nearest railway station is Howrah Junction (Kolkata) (3 km). Roads are generally good; check seasonal/monsoon conditions before high-altitude or remote stretches.

faq.q: How many days are enough for Kolkata?
faq.a: 2 days are usually enough to cover the top attractions of Kolkata at a relaxed pace.

faq.q: How much does a hotel cost in Kolkata?
faq.a: Stays in Kolkata start from ₹1,200 per night, with options across 5 price categories.

faq.q: What are the top places to visit in Kolkata?
faq.a: The top attractions are Victoria Memorial, Howrah Bridge, Dakshineswar Kali Temple.
